turns.prompt_text: what's the difference between USB type-c and Thunderbolt
turns.response_html:
To understand the difference between USB-C and Thunderbolt, it is easiest to think of USB-C as the physical shape of the connector and Thunderbolt as the high-performance technology that can run through that connector.

While they look identical, they offer different levels of speed, power, and capability.

At a Glance: Key Differences

USB-C: The Universal Connector

USB-C is an industry-standard physical connector used for charging and data. Because it is an open standard, its capabilities vary wildly depending on the device. A standard USB-C port might only support slow data transfers (USB 2.0) or basic charging, while more advanced versions like USB4 can reach speeds closer to Thunderbolt.

Thunderbolt: The Pro-Grade Protocol

Thunderbolt is a premium technology developed by Intel that uses the USB-C shape but guarantees high-end performance.

  • Speed: It offers a minimum of 40 Gbps (Thunderbolt 4) or up to 120 Gbps (Thunderbolt 5), which is significantly faster than most standard USB-C ports.
  • Video: It is designed to handle multiple high-resolution displays through a single cable.
  • Daisy-Chaining: You can connect multiple devices (like a dock, then a hard drive, then a monitor) in a single "chain" from one port.
  • PCIe Support: This allows for high-performance peripherals like external GPUs (eGPUs) and ultra-fast NVMe storage.

Compatibility Tip

A Thunderbolt port on a computer can handle almost anything you plug into it, including standard USB-C accessories. However, a standard USB-C port may not work with Thunderbolt-exclusive hardware like high-end docking stations or external graphics cards.

For professional workflows involving video editing or multiple monitors, a Thunderbolt 4 setup is the most reliable choice. For everyday charging and phone syncing, a standard USB-C cable is typically sufficient.
